positive.prompt: We're inside Herdr: fan this review out to three sub-agents in separate tabs, one each for auth, billing, and the API layer, then merge their findings
Spin up parallel agents in Herdr tabs to try three design approaches at once and compare them
Run parallel research across sub-agents, one Herdr tab per question, and synthesize what they come back with

negative.prompt: Break this spec into small verifiable tasks with acceptance criteria
Record the decision to adopt event sourcing for the orders service as an ADR

evals.prompt: HERDR_ENV=1. The user says: "Review the auth, payments, and notifications modules in parallel for ticket PROJ-42; don't change any files. Run the payments review in Codex, which has no global brain prompt installed." Fan it out.
evals.expected_output: A roster of three read-only reviewer slices, each spawned in its own tab without focus and labeled <ticket> <scope> (<persona>), briefed cold with paths, constraints, and a return shape, collected by pane id and synthesized with claims verified
expectations: Writes the roster (persona, label, self-contained brief, return shape) before creating any tab
Creates one tab per slice with --no-focus and a --label of the form <ticket> <scope> (<persona>), such as a code-reviewer persona, reading the pane id from the response rather than guessing it
The Codex tab's brief adopts the persona by telling the agent to read .agents/agents/<persona>.md, adopt it, and declare it, not with /brain or /prompts:brain
Each brief starts with the persona to adopt, the same one its tab label shows, names the paths, says not to modify files, and states the return shape; none tells the agent to exit
Starts each agent with a lowercase Herdr handle derived from the ticket and slice, such as proj-42-auth, never the label or a pane id, and does not try to give the Herdr agent the label as its name
Confirms with herdr tab get that each tab shows its PROJ-42 <scope> (<persona>) label
Prompts without --wait, then waits and reads each agent by pane id
Synthesizes and de-duplicates the findings, verifies claims before relaying them, and closes only tabs it created
